elias_vance.spread: Choose Spread when quick throws match your quarterback and receivers. Late decisions give pass rushers free shots by Week 1 and turn quick throws into interceptions.
elias_vance.west_coast: Choose West Coast when your quarterback decides fast and receivers reach their landmarks; slow reads stall drives before routes finish.
elias_vance.smashmouth: Choose Power Run when linemen and backs have first-contact jobs. Miss those jobs, and drives stall while early downs get wasted.
elias_vance.air_raid: Choose Air Raid when protection calls and quarterback hot reads are assigned before Week 1. Otherwise bigger pass plays become sacks and interceptions.
elias_vance.balanced: Choose Balanced when run, pass, and protection all need starter assignments. Miss one role, and Week 1 prep slows.
elias_vance.4-3: Choose Four-three when defensive linemen have run-defense jobs assigned before Week 1. Miss those jobs, and rushing lanes open.
elias_vance.3-4: Three-four asks linebackers to rush, cover, and stop the run. Set backup linebackers before committing, or one injury breaks the front.
elias_vance.zone_cov: Choose Cover Two to protect deep passes. Missed tackling underneath becomes free yards and longer drives.
elias_vance.balanced_d: Choose Cover Three to assign deep zones and flats now. It limits calls that leave defenders late to zones by Week 1.
elias_vance.man_press: Choose Man Press when corners have speed and the safety plan covers deep misses. Lost one-on-ones become immediate explosive plays.

derrick_coleman.spread: Choose Spread when short throws still force tackles. If yards after catch fail, drives waste possessions.
derrick_coleman.west_coast: Choose West Coast when the quarterback decides fast and receivers block. Late throws or missed blocks turn precision into Week 1 stalled drives.
derrick_coleman.smashmouth: Choose Power Run when the line and backs own first contact. Miss that contact, and the plan gets predictable by Week 1.
derrick_coleman.air_raid: Choose Air Raid when blitz pickup and quarterback hot throws are assigned by Week 1. Otherwise pressure turns tempo into sacks and turnovers.
derrick_coleman.balanced: Choose Balanced when run, pass, and protection roles all need shared game-plan decisions. Name each starter role, or Week 1 prep slows.
derrick_coleman.4-3: Choose Four-three to let defenders attack assigned gaps and zones. If gap and coverage jobs are unassigned, Week 1 mistakes arrive fast.
derrick_coleman.3-4: Choose Three-four when linebackers have pressure and coverage jobs. Miss either job, and blitzers leave easy throws behind them.
derrick_coleman.zone_cov: Choose Cover Two when safeties communicate and corners tackle. Poor communication turns short completions into long drives.
derrick_coleman.balanced_d: Choose Cover Three to keep the ball in front. Missed tackling turns long drives into points.
derrick_coleman.man_press: Choose Man Press when corners have press assignments and safeties are assigned deep coverage. Miss deep help, and one beaten corner gives up a long touchdown.

maya_alvarez.spread: Choose Spread to give skill players easier touches. If route and protection jobs are unassigned, players guess by Week 1.
maya_alvarez.west_coast: Choose West Coast when quarterback and receivers share the same quick reads. Late throws or routes stall Week 1 drives.
maya_alvarez.smashmouth: Choose Power Run when the line and backs need assigned run-game jobs. Assignments must hold up by Week 1 or early downs stall.
maya_alvarez.air_raid: Choose Air Raid when protection calls, quarterback hot reads, and receiver jobs are assigned before Week 1. Otherwise extra tempo magnifies mistakes.
maya_alvarez.balanced: Choose Balanced when several starters need touches. Assign roles now, or Week 1 calls create missed assignments.
maya_alvarez.4-3: Choose Four-three to simplify the front seven. If linemen and linebackers do not know their run lanes, Week 1 cutback runs get free yards.
maya_alvarez.3-4: Choose Three-four when linebackers have rush, coverage, and run-defense jobs. Miss one job, and Week 1 calls leave open rushing lanes.
maya_alvarez.zone_cov: Choose Cover Two to assign each safety a deep half. Missed communication still turns underneath throws into longer drives.
maya_alvarez.balanced_d: Choose Cover Three to give every defender assigned coverage rules. Missed communication still leaves free yards.
maya_alvarez.man_press: Choose Man Press when defenders own coverage without extra safety protection. Fast corners with assigned deep help get takeaway chances; without that help by Week 1, beaten corners give up long gains.

elias_vance.win_division: Choose Win Division when you will fund veteran upgrades and protect division-game starters in September. Miss early, and owner patience drops.
elias_vance.playoff_berth: Choose Playoff Berth when you will fix injuries, backup order, and trade targets before the standings gap widens. Miss early, and depth or trade questions arrive.
elias_vance.winning_record: Choose Winning Record to protect owner patience while you fix starters, injuries, and cap. Early losses shrink that patience.
elias_vance.rebuild_progress: Choose Rebuild Progress to protect young-player snaps, overpaid-contract exits, and depth growth. If snaps and exits do not happen, owner patience still falls.
elias_vance.cap_health: Choose Cap Health to protect injury replacements, extensions, trades, and next-offseason cap space.
elias_vance.star_power: Choose the high-end talent goal when staff roles, cap space, and weekly usage protect the star. Otherwise cap hits block depth and extensions.
elias_vance.no_losing_streak: Choose No Losing Streak when you will open Recap, injuries, and Game Plan after every loss. Skip that work and morale or owner patience drops.
elias_vance.draft_well: Choose Draft Well when cheap starters must replace veteran spending over the next three seasons. Miss picks, and one veteran signing cannot cover the cost.
elias_vance.championship: Championship raises every weekly deadline. Choose it when depth, cap space, and starter health cover late-season injuries and fixes without rushed trades.

derrick_coleman.win_division: Choose Win Division when early losses will trigger veteran-upgrade decisions instead of rushed lineup churn. Expect less patience for rookie mistakes.
derrick_coleman.playoff_berth: Choose Playoff Berth to chase weekly wins before rebuilding the roster. Miss early, and depth-chart or trade questions arrive fast.
derrick_coleman.winning_record: Choose Winning Record when starters need time before owner patience drops. Miss it, and owner questions hit lineup and plan choices.
derrick_coleman.rebuild_progress: Choose Rebuild Progress when young players are ready to take jobs from veterans. If no jobs change, owner patience fades.
derrick_coleman.cap_health: Choose Cap Health to keep injury replacements, extensions, and trade options open.
derrick_coleman.star_power: Choose the high-end talent goal when those players earn practice reps and game-day jobs. Otherwise their cap hits block depth moves and extensions.
derrick_coleman.no_losing_streak: No losing streak protects morale and owner patience. After one loss, open Recap, injuries, and Game Plan before the next kickoff.
derrick_coleman.draft_well: Choose Draft Well to find competitors with clear roles. Miss those role reports, and testing numbers still waste picks.
derrick_coleman.championship: Championship is the highest ownership bar. Choose it when starters, injury depth, and late-season cap space cover fixes without rushed cuts or trades.

maya_alvarez.win_division: Winning the division makes owner expectations immediate. Choose it when the plan includes veteran upgrades, protected starters, and division games as early checkpoints.
maya_alvarez.playoff_berth: Choose Playoff Berth to chase weekly wins before rebuilding the roster. Miss early, and trade or depth-chart questions arrive fast.
maya_alvarez.winning_record: Choose Winning Record to protect owner patience early. Miss early, and lineup and trade questions get louder by October.
maya_alvarez.rebuild_progress: Choose Rebuild Progress when young players earn roles and overpaid contracts have exits. Visible snaps protect owner patience through losses.
maya_alvarez.cap_health: Choose Cap Health to protect future extensions and injury replacements. Spend past that limit, and later promises force cuts, trades, or restructures.
maya_alvarez.star_power: Choose the high-end talent goal when staff roles, cap space, and weekly usage protect those players; otherwise cap hits block depth moves and extensions.
maya_alvarez.no_losing_streak: Choose No Losing Streak when you will fix Recap, injuries, and Game Plan after each loss. Miss twice and morale meetings turn into owner-patience penalties.
maya_alvarez.draft_well: Choose Draft Well when cheap starters over the next three seasons beat quick veteran fixes. Missed picks force expensive replacements.
maya_alvarez.championship: Championship sets owner expectations immediately. Choose it when starters, injuries, and late-season depth have depth-chart and medical protection.

roster_screen: Start with production against cap cost. Protect players who outperform their deals, or future extensions and injury fixes get tighter.
Name age, starter strength, and contract length before naming a three-year core; old money blocks future starters.
Name recent performance before keeping a familiar name; paying decline creates cap squeeze and uncovered depth.
depth_chart_screen: Identify which starter or backup opponents attack first; fix that role before Game Plan or cap work distracts you.
Name age and contract before choosing between close players; the older choice costs later cap space.
Start with Auto-set as a baseline, then override when the tradeoff protects snaps, development, or Week 1 prep.
cap_screen: Cap space pays for later fixes. Tie each win-now spend to a named starter, injury, trade, or extension need before those options shrink.
Preview dead money before any restructure; it removes future injury, trade, and extension options.
Choose one move that fixes a starter or backup job without draining future cap space.
game_plan_screen: Pick calls that put assigned blockers, receivers, or defenders in repeatable jobs; unsupported jobs create Week 1 mistakes.
Keep the install narrow when calls do not match current player roles; extra complexity creates Week 1 missed assignments.
When coach preference and current player roles disagree, protect this year's players; forcing the install creates Week 1 mistakes.

roster_screen: Find the players who stay effective through contact and fatigue; protect them with backups before injuries put replacements into those jobs.
Identify the thinnest backup group now; injuries turn that player into the next starter.
Name finish, effort, cap cost, and role production before keeping a player; a label without a playable role wastes snaps.
depth_chart_screen: Set starter reps for players who earn them every week; skipped backup order puts an unassigned player in after injuries.
Start the close-call player with fewer missed assignments; a starter with more missed assignments creates blown calls.
If a backup lacks a third-down job, fix that order before Advance Week.
cap_screen: Pay the difference-makers, then name the middle-of-roster deals that block cap space for starters.
Name every contract that costs more than its role before adding another player; overpaying role players steals future snaps from hungrier depth.
Preview cap savings and role snaps before cutting a contributing backup; a cut without role replacement hits morale and depth.
game_plan_screen: Pick the plan that repeats starter assignments already saved on the depth chart; ignored assignments create missed calls by kickoff.
Call power when the line and backs own first contact; otherwise pick quicker throws before missed-protection sacks rise.
Name player assignments and the first call in one sentence; if not, Week 1 speed breaks calls.

roster_screen: Keep productive players in assigned jobs; moving one without a named replacement job drops morale and wastes Week 1 snaps.
Open the roster screen to decide who needs fewer snaps, a harder role, or a new job before development stalls.
Move a productive player into a defined role; leaving him misplaced wastes snaps and slows development.
depth_chart_screen: Set every depth-chart role with a reason; unassigned jobs cost morale and development snaps.
Pair the right backup with the right starter when development snaps are the plan; an unassigned role slows a young player.
Assign small role increases after giving the young player a package, backup, or starter job; too much too soon slows development and hurts depth.
cap_screen: Name the player who gets extended, cut, or moved; a surprise cap move drops morale and blocks later injury or extension fixes.
Protect cap space for when the season changes; spending it too early limits injury and trade answers.
Name cap, role, and morale logic before moving a familiar player; no explanation hurts morale and owner patience.
game_plan_screen: Choose the scheme that fits Week 1 roles; the longest install creates mistakes when assignments lag.
Set roles the scheme explains by Week 1; unassigned jobs create missed assignments and slow drives.
Choose a scheme that names the leaders' jobs first; backups get defined jobs and fewer missed assignments.

elias_vance.intel_briefing__meet_roster: Open the roster next; name the injured starter, overpaid contract, or uncovered first-backup job before a fix spends cap space or creates a new hole.
elias_vance.meet_roster__hire_coach: Name roster questions, then hire the coach whose practice plan fixes the starter job, depth gap, or staff ownership gap you found.
elias_vance.hire_coach__hire_scout: Hire the scout who names medical limits, assigned-role gaps, and coachability warnings for the coach's scheme; incomplete reports waste future-starter picks.
elias_vance.hire_scout__set_scheme: With scouting questions covered, choose schemes that protect current starter assignments by Week 1.
elias_vance.set_scheme__depth_chart: Save schemes after naming who plays each role; unsupported depth choices expose Week 1 starter or backup assignments.
elias_vance.depth_chart__cap_strategy: Preview cap after the depth chart; lineup choices decide which injuries, trades, or extensions fit under the budget.
elias_vance.cap_strategy__set_goals: Choose goals that match budget, roster, and timeline; missed promises cut owner patience.
elias_vance.set_goals__blueprint: Open the blueprint to lock staff, roster, cap, and goal deadlines; missed weekly tasks cut owner patience.

derrick_coleman.choose_agm__intel_briefing: AGM choice is locked. Open Franchise Intel and choose the first fix: roster roles, cap space, game plan, or owner patience.

derrick_coleman.meet_roster__hire_coach: After injured starters and first-backup jobs are named, choose the coach who controls practice reps; missing accountability costs Week 1 prep.
derrick_coleman.hire_coach__hire_scout: Pick the scout who answers draft questions before deadlines; missing scout info turns picks into uncovered roster jobs.
derrick_coleman.hire_scout__set_scheme: Choose how this roster plays next; unsupported scheme calls will create Week 1 assignment mistakes.
derrick_coleman.set_scheme__depth_chart: Set starters and backups for the snaps the scheme requires; unsupported roles create Week 1 mistakes.
derrick_coleman.depth_chart__cap_strategy: Preview cap space after the lineup; injuries and extensions need cap space later.
derrick_coleman.cap_strategy__set_goals: Pick a target that matches cost, roster, and owner patience; missed goals shrink patience.
derrick_coleman.set_goals__blueprint: Name the first weekly tasks now; missed prep, uncovered backup jobs, or cap mistakes cost owner patience after Week 1.

maya_alvarez.choose_agm__intel_briefing: AGM choice is locked. Match starter, backup, cap, and owner warnings to staff, depth-chart, cap, or goal decisions before Week 1.
maya_alvarez.intel_briefing__meet_roster: Name injured starters, role conflicts, and unhappy veterans next before Depth Chart or Contracts fixes.
maya_alvarez.meet_roster__hire_coach: After injured starters, undefined roles, and contract cost are named, choose the coach who teaches the roles Week 1 needs.
maya_alvarez.hire_coach__hire_scout: Hire the scout who names assigned roles and medical limits for the coach's scheme; missing answers waste picks and slow future development.
maya_alvarez.hire_scout__set_scheme: Choose schemes that match player skills; calls without backup protection create Week 1 mistakes and morale loss.
maya_alvarez.set_scheme__depth_chart: Set starters, backups, and package jobs before Week 1; unassigned jobs create missed assignments and morale loss.
maya_alvarez.depth_chart__cap_strategy: Preview cap space after depth decisions; roster spots and injury replacements need cap space later.
maya_alvarez.cap_strategy__set_goals: Choose goals after the money and roster are honest; unsupported targets force deadline overpays and shorten owner patience.
maya_alvarez.set_goals__blueprint: Set the plan, deadlines, and miss consequences now; otherwise owner patience drops fast.

loading_tips: Choose schemes that protect Week 1 prep; a plan needing different players creates Week 1 mistakes.
Save healthy cap space for injuries, trades, and core extensions.
Save the first depth chart carefully; it decides which starter loses backup cover after an injury.
Choose a season goal the current starters back; unsupported goals force deadline overpays or shorten owner patience.
Protect players who outperform contracts; losing cheap production spends cap space on expensive replacements.
Choose a coach and scheme pair that matches current starter assignments before Week 1; forcing calls that current starters cannot handle slows prep.
Open scouting reports before draft weekend; missing reports turn a pick into a four-year roster cost.
Set practice roles clearly; unassigned reps slow development and expose players on game day.

blueprint_closing_monologue.elias_vance: Plan set: open roster cost, cap tradeoffs, and first deadlines every week. Miss those fixes, and the next injury, extension, or uncovered backup job erases a win streak.
blueprint_closing_monologue.derrick_coleman: Plan set: assign staff, scheme, goals, and next-week tasks. Miss prep, depth, or cap choices and Week 1 starts with missed assignments, uncovered backup jobs, or blocked fixes.
blueprint_closing_monologue.maya_alvarez: Plan set: name who plays, what must be fixed each week, and which owner promises are live. If jobs stay unassigned, morale drops and owner patience falls by midseason.
